summary: A 1941 CCC-built Aermotor tower in Birmingham's Ruffner Mountain Nature Preserve, unique in Alabama for its rooftop platform.

facts.design: 100-ft steel Aermotor MC-39 tower with a 7x7 ft cab and a rooftop observation platform, added originally to carry an aircraft beacon; the only lookout in Alabama built with this rooftop option
facts.agency: City of Birmingham and Birmingham Board of Education

access.note: Located in the City of Birmingham's Ruffner Mountain Nature Preserve, a public park with 14+ miles of trails; as of a 2016 report the tower itself was not open and there was only talk of restoring it for public use.

events.note: 100-ft Aermotor MC-39 built by the Civilian Conservation Corps on Ruffner Mountain
Registered as US 870 / AL 49 on January 18, 2010, nominated by Thomas Kaufmann

evidence.supports: only lookout in Alabama with a rooftop observation platform
evidence.quote: Wharton Lookout Tower is the only lookout in Alabama with a rooftop observation platform.

evidence.supports: rooftop deck was an Aermotor 7x7 cab option, unusual in the South, added here for an aircraft beacon
evidence.quote: This was an option for Aermotor 7'x7' cabs, and is found in some mid-Atlantic states, but very unusual in the south. It is on this tower because the FM once had an aircraft beacon on the roof.

evidence.supports: built 1941, 100' MC-39 Aermotor, built by the CCC
evidence.quote: this is a 100' MC-39 Aermotor built by the CCC in 1941.

evidence.supports: 100-ft galvanized steel tower erected 1941 by the CCC near East Lake
evidence.quote: the Wharton Lookout Tower (also called East Lake Tower) is a 100-foot tall galvanized steel frame fire lookout tower erected in 1941 by the Civilian Conservation Corps on Ruffner Mountain near East Lake in what is now the Ruffner Mountain Nature Preserve

evidence.supports: administered by City of Birmingham and Board of Education; cooperators AFC and Ruffner Mountain Nature Center
evidence.quote: City of Birmingham, Birmingham Board of Education, Alabama Forestry Commission, and Ruffner Mountain Nature Center

evidence.supports: as of 2016, talk of refurbishing the tower for public use; not yet open
evidence.quote: Several years ago, there was talk about refurbishing the tower for public use.

evidence.supports: former executive director gave a presentation on the tower's restoration potential
evidence.quote: Check out this 2013 video of former Ruffner Mountain Executive Director Robbie Fearn giving a presentation on the tower’s potential restoration.
1,038 acres (4.20 km 2 ) nature preserve located in the eastern portion of Jefferson County, Alabama

evidence.supports: preserve has more than 14 miles of hiking trails
evidence.quote: The preserve contains more than 14 miles (23 km) of hiking trails.

sources.title: A Birmingham treasure - the Ruffner Mountain fire lookout tower

notes_for_editor: No source documents staffing history, when fire-watch use ended, or whether the 2013-2016 restoration talk ever resulted in the tower being opened to climbers; current access/climbable status should be verified before publishing a stronger claim. The eastern_us_lookouts cache page (easternuslookouts.weebly.com/wharton.html) was checked but contains only the tower name, county, and preserve name with no additional prose, so it was not cited.
